subject: Novus AI activation agenda & fallbacks for GPU pool
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@novusai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel@novusai.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novus AI activation: baseline, regions, and go-live window

Hi Marcus / Monica —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We got internal buy-in and want to start planning activation for a reserved GPU pool for our inference traffic. High level details below — attaching our requirements doc and a simple network diagram.

Summary:
- Expected peak qps (gen calls): ~140 requests/sec (95th percentile). Typical payloads ~600 tokens.
- Primary region: us-west (preferred); secondary region: eu-west as DR.
- SLA target: p99 < 300ms on gen paths; acceptable fallback to smaller model with slightly higher latency during burst events.
- We anticipate large batch runs overnight for embeddings (lower latency needs) and daytime interactive generation (low latency).

Asks:
1) Initial recommended pool size (gpus + model shard layout) and a proposal for autoscale/burst policy (warm pool vs on-demand burst).
2) Suggested go-live windows (we're aiming for late April but can be flexible).
3) Any network peering prerequisites or IP allowlist requirements for our VPC.

Attachments: NovusAI_REQUIREMENTS_v2.pdf, network-diagram.png

Can we schedule a 45-minute kickoff next week to lock the mutual action plan?

Best,
Elena
VP Product, Novus AI
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novusai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus AI activation: baseline, regions, and go-live window

Elena —

Thanks for the clear requirements and the diagram. Happy to run a kickoff and propose a concrete MAP. Quick responses inline and a proposed path forward:

Quick answers:
- Proposed baseline: 8x A10G-equivalent GPUs in us-west (sharded across 2 nodes, baseline pool = 6 GPUs warm, 2 GPU reserve for burst). eu-west: 2x GPUs for DR/warm standby.
- Autoscale recommendation: target-based autoscale with a warm pool floor (60% of baseline) and a controlled burst cap at 2x baseline for short windows. See attached initial-capacity-estimate.xlsx for numbers.
- Network: standard VPC peering + IP allowlist; we will need a list of your outbound ranges and a contact for netops.

Proposed kickoff agenda (45 min):
1) Confirm final qps and token distributions (ops will bring telemetry assumptions)
2) Agree pool topology and failover plan (regional priorities)
3) Autoscale & burst thresholds, KV cache warming strategy
4) Pre-prod validation tests and success criteria
5) Timeline and owners (contracts / peering / runbooks)

Provisional timeline:
- Kickoff: next Wed 10:00 PT
- Final MAP & capacity estimate: +4 business days after kickoff
- Netops peering & contract: ~2 weeks concurrent
- Go-live target: Apr 26 (flexible)

Questions for you before kickoff:
- Any blackout dates in late April?
- Do you require data residency guarantees for EU traffic?

Attachments: initial-capacity-estimate.xlsx

I'll book the kickoff after we confirm a time slot. Monica will act as CS lead; Rishi and Laura will own runbook & netops respectively.

—Marcus
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novusai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus AI activation: baseline, regions, and go-live window

Elena / team —

Adding a few ops-focused notes to set expectations for the autoscale and warm/cache behavior:

Operational notes:
- KV cache warm-up: For generative latency targets at 600 tokens, expect ~5–7 minutes to stabilize latency when scaling from cold. We'll implement prefix caching for common prompts during the ramp window.
- Burst policy: Recommend capped burst (2x baseline) with a 15-minute minimum sustain window and an exponential backoff for subsequent bursts within the same 6-hour period to prevent runaway costs.
- Pre-warm strategy: schedule a rolling pre-warm (30–45 minutes) before known peak windows — we can wire this to a cron-based trigger from your traffic scheduler.
- Embeddings runs: route large batch embedding jobs to a separate queue and schedule them to off-peak windows (we can lock dedicated GPUs overnight).

Network/DR notes for Laura: cross-region failover will add ~60–120ms RTT to the p99; we should add that to Novus SLAs and test performance degradation paths.

I'll prepare a short ops runbook draft for the kickoff that includes escalation paths and expected token/unit cost at baseline vs burst.

—Rishi
Principal Infra Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena.park@novusai.com>

Thanks Marcus / Rishi — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- We have a planned marketing push the week of Apr 28, so the earlier go-live window (Apr 20–26) would be ideal — if we can validate p99 < 350ms in staging by Apr 19 we'll be comfortable.
- Data residency: EU traffic must be processed in eu-west exclusively for EU customers. US traffic can be us-west.
- Netops contact: Daniel Cho (daniel@novusai.com), he can share outbound IP ranges and peering details.

Can you also provide a rough monthly cost delta for baseline vs 2x burst so we can short-list with finance? If possible, put a line item for pre-warm run costs.

Also please open a support ticket / Jira so we can track tasks: our PM asked for a ticket ID.

Thanks — booking the kickoff for Wed 16 Mar 10:00 PT unless I hear otherwise.

Best,
Elena
